children: As the dust from Brazil's election settles, incumbent President Lula faces pressing economic challenges, says Moody's Analytics' Alfredo Coutino. The economy is fatigued, with growth slowing amid weak investment, mounting fiscal imbalances and high inflation. Economic stabilization and fiscal consolidation will be necessary to put the economy on a more sustainable path in the medium term, Coutino writes. Persistently high interest rates--necessary to fight inflation--and increased spending on social programs have worsened fiscal imbalances. The fiscal deficit doubled to an estimated 9% of GDP in 2026 from 2022, while public debt rose by 5 ppts of GDP to an estimated 83%. Moody's Analytics' baseline expects economic growth in 2027 and easing inflation, though estimates can be fine-tuned once the 2027 economic program is released. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
